tam_derivation.global_dc_market_note: Global DC market ~$280B estimated from Precedence Research headline figure; EU at $52B = 18.6% of global. EU advisory TAM = $750M × 18.6% = $140M ≈ €130M. Adjusted upward to €175M to reflect EU's higher advisory intensity per MW due to regulatory complexity (EU Taxonomy, energy-permit fragmentation across 27 jurisdictions).
tam_derivation.verdict: Conservative floor €130M; adjusted estimate €175M. This covers professional advisory fees paid annually by EU DC developers, hyperscalers, and infrastructure funds for site selection and pre-feasibility work.

sam_derivation.active_siting_decisions_per_year: 25–65 new-build/expansion projects (derived: 655 MW 2024 new supply ÷ 10–30 MW avg project size)
sam_derivation.calculation: 45 decisions × €250K avg pre-feasibility + 40 fund screenings × €80K = €11.25M + €3.2M = ~€15M direct. Full pre-feasibility advisory market (incl. upstream) estimated at €40–60M. Mid-point €50M.
sam_derivation.scope_note: SAM = the pre-feasibility and site-screening phase only. Excludes transaction advisory, DD, permitting, financial modelling — phases our tool does not replace.

som_derivation.year1: 8 enterprise subscribers × €80K/yr avg + 100 ad-hoc queries × €2.5K avg = €0.64M + €0.25M = €0.9M
som_derivation.benchmark: 1–8% SAM capture in years 1–3 is standard for B2B data/intelligence SaaS targeting a specialized professional buyer (cf. MSCI real estate analytics, Green Street Advisors, CoStar early growth phase).

pricing_models.name: Per-Query
pricing_models.description: Single siting analysis, paid upfront. Client sets load (MW), carbon ceiling, cost priority. Tool returns ≥3 ranked EU sites with supply mix and trade-off narrative. No subscription required.
pricing_models.price_logic: <20 MW → €1,500; 20–100 MW → €3,000; >100 MW hyperscale → €5,000. Benchmark: B2B geospatial intelligence queries (Orbital Insight, Carto enterprise) at $3K–15K/analysis. Our pricing anchors well below that given narrower scope.
pricing_models.target_buyer: Infrastructure fund analyst doing one-off due diligence; DC developer evaluating a single expansion market; consultant running a preliminary scan before engaging full advisory
pricing_models.pros: Zero friction, immediate activation, virality via shareable output

pricing_models.name: Annual Subscription (Tiered)
pricing_models.description: Pre-paid query credits + platform access. Starter (10 queries/yr), Pro (50 queries/yr + API access), Enterprise (unlimited + white-glove support + custom scoring weights).
pricing_models.price_logic: Starter €18K (€1,800/query effective vs €3,000 per-query = 40% saving); Pro €60K; Enterprise €180K. Discount structure incentivises annual commit. Benchmark: JLL data center market research subscriptions estimated €30K–80K/yr; MSCI real estate analytics €30K–100K/yr.
pricing_models.target_buyer: Active DC developers running ≥5 site assessments/yr; infrastructure funds with rolling portfolio evaluation; DC advisory boutiques using tool to accelerate client work
pricing_models.pros: Predictable ARR, upsell path from per-query users, justifies sales investment
pricing_models.cons: Requires proof-of-value before annual commit; longer sales cycle

pricing_models.name: Enterprise / White-Label API
pricing_models.description: Private API deployment or co-branded output for advisory firms (CBRE, JLL, C&W) embedding the engine into internal tooling, or hyperscalers wanting unlimited access with custom data overlays.
pricing_models.price_logic: Turns major advisory firms from competitors into distribution partners. CBRE manages >700 DC sites globally (Bisnow, confirmed); internal grid-analytics tooling at this scale commands six-figure licensing. Hyperscalers (AWS €8.8B EU investment announced) have internal siting teams that benefit from standardized EU grid scoring.
pricing_models.target_buyer: CBRE / JLL / C&W DC advisory practices; hyperscaler infrastructure planning teams (AWS, Microsoft, Google)
pricing_models.pros: High ACV, low churn, credibility via enterprise logo
pricing_models.cons: 6–12 month sales cycle, dependency risk on single large client

competitors.name: CBRE Data Center Solutions
competitors.what_they_do: Full-service DC site selection, leasing, transaction brokerage, and asset management. Globally dominant — managed >700 DC sites as of 2024. Data center contribution grew from 3% to 10% of CBRE total earnings between 2021 and 2024; $9B in North American DC transactions in 2024 alone.
competitors.fee_structure: Project retainer + success fee. Fees not publicly disclosed; derived from general CRE advisory benchmarks at 0.5–1.5% of deal value. For a €100M EU DC project that implies €500K–1.5M total engagement; pre-feasibility phase estimated at €150K–500K.
competitors.fee_source: Bisnow (confirmed fetch): 'None of the five major brokerages provided much additional commentary' on fee breakdown. CBRE earnings figure from same article.
competitors.gap: Weeks-to-months timeline. No self-service. Minimum deal size excludes smaller developers. Deliverable is a bespoke PowerPoint, not an auditable data product. No real-time nodal grid headroom, no EU carbon intensity (Ember) integration, no PPA-opportunity scoring.

competitors.name: Cushman & Wakefield — Data Center Advisory Group (dcsiteselection.com)
competitors.what_they_do: Dedicated DC advisory practice (own brand: dcsiteselection.com). Power-first site selection, PPA procurement, lease negotiation, sustainability consulting across EMEA. Explicitly markets 'power-first site selection strategies amid rising hyperscale demand and grid constraints' (as of Feb 2026).
competitors.fee_structure: Same consultant model as CBRE. Fees not disclosed.
competitors.fee_source: Bisnow (confirmed fetch). C&W description from openpr.com market report (confirmed fetch).
competitors.gap: Identical model constraints to CBRE. Carbon scoring is qualitative/country-level, not nodal. No EU grid congestion quantification. Each engagement bespoke — not repeatable or auditable.

competitors.name: JLL Data Centers
competitors.what_they_do: DC market research reports, tenant representation, capital markets advisory. DC portfolio is ~10% of JLL's Real Estate Management Services group. Publishes EMEA quarterly reports tracking MW supply/demand. Confirmed EU DC investment data: colo real-estate transactions doubled to $2.34B in 2023.
competitors.fee_structure: Research subscriptions estimated €30K–80K/yr; transaction advisory at % of deal.
competitors.fee_source: JLL article (confirmed fetch) for investment figures. Subscription estimate derived from peer benchmarks (JLL does not publish subscription pricing).
competitors.gap: Research product is backward-looking (what happened in the market) not forward-looking (where to build next). No power mix optimization. Advisory arm has same human-hours bottleneck. Cannot run real-time carbon or grid-headroom queries.

competitors.name: datacenterHawk
competitors.what_they_do: Platform tracking colocation availability and pricing: who has existing capacity, at what price, in which market. Serves DC investors, operators, and enterprise users via web interface, REST API, or custom data exports. Covers North America primarily; European markets (London, Frankfurt) also listed but less depth. Acquired by Simplify Compliance (2022).
competitors.fee_structure: SaaS subscription; no public pricing. Crunchbase: founded 2014.
competitors.fee_source: datacenterHawk platform page (confirmed fetch). Crunchbase entry.
competitors.gap: Answers 'where can I rent colocation space today' not 'where should I build'. No grid topology, no carbon intensity layer, no PPA-opportunity scoring. EU coverage thin vs. North America. Not designed for greenfield siting or supply-mix optimization.

competitors.name: Site Selection Group
competitors.what_they_do: Data-driven DC site selection advisory, consulting engagements for enterprise and DC developer clients. US-primary market focus with some international coverage.
competitors.fee_structure: Consulting engagement; fee not disclosed. Estimated $80K–300K range based on firm size and scope.
competitors.fee_source: siteselectiongroup.com (public website). Fee estimate is analyst-derived, not confirmed from disclosed contract.
competitors.gap: Consulting model — manual, slow, expensive. US-centric. No EU-specific grid or carbon data. Not scalable for EU multi-country comparison. No self-service.

competitors.name: Internal analyst / Excel workflow
competitors.what_they_do: Most EU DC developers and infrastructure funds run pre-feasibility with internal teams manually pulling ENTSO-E data, Ember CSVs, JLL/CBRE country reports, and ad-hoc consultant calls. Build bespoke Excel models per project.
competitors.fee_structure: Analyst time: 4–12 weeks × 1–2 FTE at EU analyst salary €60K–120K/yr → €12K–55K in labour per multi-country screening. Plus external consultant call costs.
competitors.fee_source: Derived estimate. JLL: EU colo take-up grew 19% YoY (2023) implying growing decision volume with limited tooling available.
competitors.gap: Slowest option. No standardised scoring across 27 EU jurisdictions. Requires specialist grid knowledge on staff. Cannot refresh for changing grid conditions. Results not reproducible or auditable between decisions.

our_differentiation.summary: First EU SaaS tool combining real-time grid headroom (PyPSA-Eur), hourly carbon intensity (Ember), connectivity (OSM), and PPA-opportunity scoring — returning ranked sites with power mix in <30 seconds at €1,500–5,000/query vs. €150K+ for a consultant engagement.
key_moats: Speed: <30s vs 4–12 weeks — qualitatively different decision cycle
Cost: 1/30th–1/100th of consultant retainer — opens market to sub-€500M infrastructure funds and SME DC developers
EU-specific: 20+ country grid topology via PyPSA-Eur + Ember carbon intensity — no competitor combines these
Power mix output: grid/PPA/on-site blend per site is quantified, not qualitative — a capability gap confirmed across all competitors surveyed
Carbon-first design: hard carbon-intensity constraint aligns with EU Taxonomy Article 6 disclosures and corporate net-zero commitments — compliance layer no competitor provides
Auditability: explainable scoring, not a black-box consultant opinion — repeatable, comparable across decisions
